bull.b: Gross margin reaching 81.3% and guidance for 81%–83%, versus 73.5% a year earlier, indicates stronger unit economics. If maintained, the high-margin model gives future incremental revenue greater contribution potential, supporting reinvestment and a path toward better operating leverage.

Two consecutive quarters of sequential growth, expected launches, and a Tier 1 extension indicate a developing commercial pipeline. SafePath Connect and SDK/API traction also broaden the addressable market beyond existing carrier deployments, if execution follows.

Q2 GAAP operating expenses fell 68% year over year, while non-GAAP expenses declined 26% and 8% sequentially. This leaner cost base can reduce the revenue needed to support operations and improve scalability, although resources are planned for pipeline delivery.

bear.b: Revenue fell from $58.4M in 2021 to $16.9M TTM, while Q2 and year-to-date 2026 revenue also declined year over year. This sustained contraction signals reduced scale and makes recovery dependent on converting launches and contracts into durable customer revenue.

Operating and free cash flow remain negative at $9.0M TTM, and cash generation has been below zero in every year shown. Persistent outflows reduce financial flexibility, increase dependence on external funding or receipts, and make a durable return to profitability more urgent.

Reliance on large carrier relationships concentrates commercial execution around a limited group of customers and their deployment schedules. Delays or weaker win rates could materially affect revenue timing and scale, while competition may pressure pricing and make pipeline conversion less predictable.
